Rashi on Shabbat 29b:10:1.hebrew: דומיא דכסא - קטנים, ובהא הוא דאסר רבי יהודה, אבל בגדולים שרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:10:1.english: Similar to a chair - Small [ones]; and it is in this [case] that Rabbi Yehuda prohibits, but with large [ones], he permits.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:10:2.hebrew: כסא דומיא דמטה - גדולים, ובהא הוא דשרי רבי שמעון, אבל בקטנים אסר:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:10:2.english: A chair, similar to a bed - [Both are] large, and it is in this [case] that Rabbi Shimon permits, but in [the case of] small [ones], he prohibits.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:11:1.hebrew: מוכרין כדרכן - כסות של כלאים, לובשו בשוק כדי להראותו למוכרו; דלא אסרה תורה אלא לבישה שהיא להתחמם, כדרך כל הלובשים, והעלאה דומיא דלבישה — נמי דמיתהני בה:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:11:1.english: They may sell [them] in their usual manner - A garment of diverse kinds [kilayim] — he may wear it in the marketplace in order to display it to sell it, for the Torah prohibited only wearing that is to warm oneself in the manner of all wearers; and placing [it] upon oneself is similar to wearing — [it is] also [prohibited only] when one derives benefit from it.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:11:2.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יתכוין כו' - ור' שמעון הוא דאזיל בתר כוונה:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:11:2.english: As long as he does not intend, etc. - And it is Rabbi Shimon who follows intention.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:11:3.english: And the modest [people] - Upright [people] who distance themselves from any crooked speech.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:11:4.hebrew: והא הכא דאפשר - לכל אדם למעבד שלא על ידי איסור, ואפילו הכי שרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:11:4.english: And here, where it is possible - For any person to act without [incurring] a prohibition, and even so, it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:1.hebrew: מפני נכרים - כגון פרסיים, שהיה להם יום חג שאין מניחין אור אלא בבית עבודת אלילים שלהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:1.english: Due to gentiles - Such as Persians, who had a festival day [on which] they would not permit a light [to burn] except in their house of idol worship.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:2.english: And due to thieves - So that they will not see that there is a person there and come upon him.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:3.hebrew: ומפני רוח רעה - הבאה עליו, וכשאינו רואה — נוח לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:3.english: And due to an evil spirit - That comes upon him, and when he does not see, it is a relief to him.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:4.english: [He is] exempt - And in the Gemara, it explains all of it.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:5.hebrew: כחס על הנר - שראוהו שמתקלקל, וחס עליו, וכבה את הפתילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:5.english: As [one who] spares the lamp - That he saw it becoming damaged, and spared it, and extinguished the wick.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:7.english: [He is] liable - [The Gemara] explains it.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:8.english: Exempts in all of them - This is explained in the Gemara (daf 31b).

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:9.hebrew: שהוא עושה פחם - בכיבוי זה, והוי מלאכה הצריכה לגופה, כדאמר בגמרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:12:9.english: Because he makes [it into] charcoal - Through this extinguishing, and it is a labor performed for its own sake, as [the Gemara] says in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:1:1.english: [If] he placed it in a box - He revealed his intention that it is significant to him.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:1:2.hebrew: במגוד - קביל"א, דגרע מקופסא ועדיף מאחורי הדלת, ואחורי הדלת עדיף מזרקו לאשפה. ומוכן דר' אליעזר היינו קופסא, ושלא מן המוכן — מגוד ואחורי הדלת:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:1:2.english: On a dryer - Cheville [a peg], which is inferior to [placing it in] a box and superior to [placing it] behind the door; and [placing it] behind the door is superior to having thrown it into the garbage dump. And Rabbi Eliezer's [understanding of] “prepared” is [in] a box, and “not from that which is prepared” is [on] a dryer and behind the door.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:1:3.hebrew: ומאי קרי ליה שלא מן המוכן - הואיל ולרבי אליעזר חשיב לקבולי טומאה — דלגבי קופסא לאו מוכן הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:1:3.english: And what is the reason that he called it “not prepared”? - Since according to Rabbi Eliezer it is considered [significant enough] to receive ritual impurity — [the Gemara explains that] relative to a box, it is not prepared.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:1:4.hebrew: ורבי יהושע סבר כו' - ומוכן דרבי יהושע — מגוד ואחורי הדלת, ושלא מן המוכן — זרקו לאשפה:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:1:4.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua held, etc. - And [the case of] "prepared" according to Rabbi Yehoshua is [hanging it on] a dryer and [placing it] behind the door, and "not from that which is prepared" is [where] he threw it into the garbage dump.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:1:5.hebrew: ומאי קרי ליה - למגוד מוכן, הואיל ולר' יהושע בטל? דלגבי אשפה דאיירי בה רבי יהושע, מוכן הוא. ורבי עקיבא — תלאו במגוד קרי מוכן, ואחורי הדלת שלא מן המוכן:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:1:5.english: And why does he call it - [hanging it] on a peg "prepared," seeing that according to Rabbi Yehoshua it is nullified? [Because] relative to the garbage dump that Rabbi Yehoshua was dealing with, it is prepared. And Rabbi Akiva calls hanging it on a peg "prepared," and [placing it] behind the door "not prepared."

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:2:1.hebrew: והדר ביה ר' עקיבא לגבי ר' יהושע - ומטהר אף במוכן:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:2:1.english: And Rabbi Akiva retracted [his opinion] in favor of Rabbi Yehoshua - And deems [it] pure even [in the case of that which is] prepared.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:2:2.hebrew: מדקתני - במתניתין פתילת הבגד, דמשמע שעדיין בגד הוא קצת וחשבו בעיניו, ואפ"ה קאמר רבי עקיבא במתני' טהורה היא — אלמא הדר ביה:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:2:2.english: From that which it teaches - In the Mishnah, "the wick of the garment," which implies that it is still somewhat a garment and he considered it [significant] in his eyes, and nevertheless Rabbi Akiva says in the Mishnah, "It is ritually pure" — evidently he retracted [his opinion].

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:2:3.hebrew: של בגד - משמע שקפלה מבגד. ״הבגד״ משמע שקפל הבגד עצמו שלם. ולענין הדלקה — כדאוקימנא לעיל טעמא דרבי אליעזר, דבעי פתילה מחורכת שתדלק יפה:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:2:3.english: Of a garment - [This] implies that he folded it from a garment, [whereas] “the garment” implies that he folded the garment itself whole. And with regard to lighting — [it is] as we established above: Rabbi Eliezer’s reason is that he requires a singed wick so that it will burn well.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:3:1.hebrew: שתהא מנטפת - ויתקיים הנר, שתהא השמן מטפטף כל שעה לתוך הנר. וטעמא — משום גזרה שמא יסתפק הימנו; וכיון שהקצהו לנר, חייב משום מכבה. ואפי' אותה שפופרת של חרס, דמאיסא ליה — גזרינן:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:3:1.english: So that it will drip - And the lamp will be sustained, that the oil will drip constantly into the lamp. And the reason [for the prohibition] is due to a decree lest one take [oil] from it; and since he designated it for the lamp, [one who takes from it] is liable for extinguishing. And even [in the case of] that earthenware tube, which is repulsive to him, we decree.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:3:2.hebrew: אבל אם חיברה - ליכא למיחש, דמשום איסור שבת בדיל מיניה:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:3:2.english: However, if [the craftsman] attached it - There is no reason to be concerned [lest he take from it], for because of the prohibition of Shabbat, he keeps away from it.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:3:3.hebrew: ויתן ראש הפתילה - השני, שהוא יוצא דרך הנקב האחר שבנר לשאוב, ושמן נמשך דרך הפתילה לראש הדולק:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:3:3.english: And place the head of the wick - The second [end], which emerges through the other hole in the lamp to draw [oil], and oil is drawn through the wick to the burning end.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:3:4.english: And Rabbi Yehuda permits - For he does not issue a decree [lest one take from it].

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:4:1.hebrew: דלא מיפסק - מידי, שהוא מונח בתוך חלל הנר, למעלה מכיסוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:4:1.english: That it is not separated - [By] anything, as it is placed within the cavity of the lamp, above the cover.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:4:2.hebrew: דמפסקא - שהרי אצל הנר מונחת, ויש כאן הפסק, וליכא למימר גופיה הוא — אימא מודה דנגזור:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:4:2.english: Which is separate - For behold, it is placed next to the lamp and there is a separation here, and one cannot say [that] it is [part of the lamp] itself; say [therefore] that he agrees that we should decree [a prohibition].

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:5:1.hebrew: תנא אם חיברה - בעה"ב עצמו מבעוד יום, בסיד או בחרסית — מותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:5:1.english: It was taught: If he attached it - [Even if] the homeowner himself [attached it] while it was still day, with plaster or with potter’s clay, it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:5:2.english: Similar to a craftsman - That he attached it well.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:7:1.hebrew: דשישא - רצפה של שיש, דלא עביד בה חריץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:7:1.english: Of marble - A marble floor, where [dragging] does not make a furrow.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:7:3.hebrew: כדשתיקו ליה חבריא - רבי טרפון וזקנים — שמפני שלא אמרו לו דבר, דימה והעיד דמותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:7:3.english: As the colleagues were silent to him - Rabbi Tarfon and the Elders — for since they did not say anything to him, he assumed and testified that it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:7:4.hebrew: נפק מיניה חורבה - וינהגו היתר בדבר. ור' יצחק סבירא ליה כרבי יהודה, דדבר שאין מתכוין אסור; ואע"ג דבשייש לא עביד חריץ — גזר אטו עיליתא דעלמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:7:4.english: Damage will result from it - And [people] will treat the matter as permitted. And Rabbi Yitzḥak holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, that an unintentional act is prohibited; and even though on marble it does not make a furrow, he decreed [it] due to an ordinary upper story.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:8:1.hebrew: ריש כנישתא - מפטיר כנסיות, המכניס ומוציא ומיישב תלמידים ותינוקות:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:8:1.english: The Head of the Kenesset - The one who dismisses assemblies, who ushers in and out, and seats students and children.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:8:2.hebrew: דבצרה - שם מקום, "כי זבח לה' בבצרה" (ישעיהו ל״ד:ו׳):
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:8:2.english: Of Batzra - The name of a place, [as in]: "For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah" (Isaiah 34:6).

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:8:3.english: In accordance with Rabbi Shimon - Who said: A person may drag a bed, chair, or bench.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:8:4.hebrew: דלא אפשר - אלא בגרירה, שאין יכול ליטלן בידו:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:8:4.english: Where it is not possible - Except by dragging, as one cannot carry them in his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:8:5.hebrew: מחלוקת בקטנים - ואע"ג דאפשר בטלטול — שרי רבי שמעון, הואיל ואין מתכוין לחריץ; ור' יהודה סבר: כיון דאפשר — אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:8:5.english: The dispute is in the case of small [benches] - And even though it is possible [to move them] by carrying, Rabbi Shimon permits [dragging them], since he does not intend [to make] a furrow; and Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] since it is possible, it is forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 29b:9:2.hebrew: וקתני קטנים - כסא. ורבי יהודה פליג עליה, דתנן במסכת ביצה: רבי יהודה אומר כל הכלים אין נגררים. דאי לאו משום פלוגתייהו, למה לי למיתני גדולים? השתא קטנים שרי רבי שמעון, גדולים מיבעיא? אלא, תנא קטנים משום ר' שמעון, ותנא גדולים משום רבי יהודה:
Rashi on Shabbat 29b:9:2.english: And it teaches small [objects] - A chair. And Rabbi Yehuda disagrees with him, as we learned in a mishna in tractate Beitzah: Rabbi Yehuda says: No utensils may be dragged. For were it not for their dispute, why do I need [the tanna] to teach large [objects]? Now [that] Rabbi Shimon permits small [objects], is [it] necessary [to state that he permits] large [objects]? Rather, [the tanna] taught small [objects] on account of Rabbi Shimon, and taught large [objects] on account of Rabbi Yehuda.

Tosafot on Shabbat 29b:11:1.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יתכוין בחמה מפני החמה וכו' - ובענין דלא הוי פסיק רישיה, כגון שהוא לבוש מלבושים אחרים להגין עליו מפני החמה ומפני הצינה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 29b:11:1.english: “As long as he does not intend in the sun [for protection] from the sun, etc.” - And [this is] in a situation where it is not a pesik reishei, such as where he is wearing other garments to protect him from the sun and from the cold.

Tosafot on Shabbat 29b:7:1.hebrew: גזירה עיליתא דשישא אטו עיליתא דעלמא - והא דקאמר בסוף המצניע (לקמן שבת דף צה. ושם): אמימר שרא זילחא במחוזא, ומפרש: דטעמא מאי אמור רבנן? דילמא אתי לאשוויי גומות, הכא ליכא גומות; ומפרש בקונטרס דכולה מחוזא רצפה היתה — התם אין לגזור מחוזא אטו שאר עיירות, אבל בעיר אחת גזרינן עלייה זו אטו עלייה אחרת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 29b:7:1.english: A decree [on] a marble upper story on account of a standard upper story - And as for that which [the Gemara] says at the end of [the chapter] HaMatzni'a (below, Shabbat 95a and there), [that] Ameimar permitted sprinkling [water] in Meḥoza, and [the Gemara] explains: What is the reason the Rabbis said [that it is forbidden]? Lest one come to level depressions; here, there are no depressions; and the Kuntres explains that the whole of Meḥoza was paved — there, we do not issue a decree [on] Meḥoza on account of other cities, but within a single city, we decree this upper story on account of another upper story.

Tosafot on Shabbat 29b:8:1.hebrew: ה"ג: מחלוקת בקטנים, אבל בגדולים ד"ה מותר - ול"ג: "ד"ה אסור" — דבפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כ: ושם) משמע דטפי שרי היכא דלא אפשר מהיכא דאפשר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 29b:8:1.english: This is the correct reading: "The dispute is in the case of small [benches], but in the case of large [benches], everyone agrees that it is permitted" - And we do not read: "Everyone agrees that it is forbidden" — for in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 20b, and there), it implies that it is more [readily] permitted where it is impossible [to do otherwise] than where it is possible.
